title: Engine stalls while driving
h1: Why does my car shut off while driving?
metaDesc: Engine stalled or shut off while driving? Answer a few quick questions to narrow down fuel, electrical or sensor causes, and what to do before driving again.
synonyms: car shut off on the highway
intro: When the engine shuts off while you're moving, you lose power steering and most of your brake assist, so this is a safety problem even if it restarts. What you noticed right before it died is the best clue. Answer the questions below to narrow it down and see what to do next.
safety: If the engine dies while you're moving, turn on your hazard lights, shift to neutral, keep steering and press the brake firmly, and steer to the shoulder. Steering and braking can take much more force than usual.
If the temperature gauge is in the red, you see steam, or the oil light came on, don't restart it.
If you smell raw fuel or see smoke, get everyone out and away from the car.
If it stalls once, don't rely on it in traffic or on the highway until it's diagnosed.

q_warning.q: Right before or as it died, did you notice any of these?

opts.a: Temperature gauge in the red, steam, or a hot smell
Oil pressure light, or loud knocking from the engine
Battery light on, or lights and gauges dimmed or flickered
Sputtering, shaking, loss of power, or a flashing check engine light
Nothing like that. It just shut off
Suddenly, like flipping a switch, with no sputter
It sputtered, surged or lost power first
When I hit a bump or my knee bumped the key or key ring

q_fuel.q: What was the fuel gauge showing?

opts.a: Near empty, or the low fuel light was on
Yes, it restarts and runs normally, sometimes only after cooling down
No, it cranks but won't start
No, it won't crank and the dash went dark

result.title: The engine may have overheated and shut down
result.now: Don't restart it. Let it cool for at least 30 minutes with the hood closed, then have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see coolant leaking or the reservoir is empty once cool, a leak or failed hose is likely. Mention it when you call.
Never open the radiator cap on a hot engine. Hot coolant can spray out.
If the oil pressure light came on or the engine knocked, tell the shop. Don't restart it.
result.why: An engine that gets hot enough to stall can warp or crack parts. Restarting it, or driving even a short distance, can turn a hose or thermostat repair into a major engine repair.

causes.name: Coolant leak or low coolant
causes.clues: A sweet smell, steam, or a puddle under the front of the car.

causes.name: Failed cooling fan or water pump
causes.clues: It overheated in traffic or with the A/C on.

causes.name: Head gasket damage
causes.clues: White exhaust smoke or coolant loss with no visible leak.

you: Once fully cool, check the coolant reservoir level.
Look for leaks under the car.
shop: Cooling fan and water pump check

result.title: The engine may have lost oil pressure
result.now: Don't restart it. Check the oil level on the dipstick, then have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the oil is very low, adding oil won't undo any damage. Have it checked before running it.
If the engine was knocking loudly before it stopped, it may be seriously damaged.
result.why: Oil keeps metal parts from grinding against each other. When pressure drops, damage happens fast, and an engine that stalls with knocking may have seized. Restarting it can make the damage much worse.

causes.name: Very low oil level
causes.clues: An overdue oil change, oil leaks, or burning oil smell.

causes.name: Failed oil pump or blocked oil pickup
causes.clues: The oil level is fine but the light came on.

causes.name: Internal engine damage
causes.clues: Loud knocking before it died.

you: Check the oil level on the dipstick with the engine off.
shop: Oil pressure test with a gauge
Check whether the engine turns freely by hand

result.title: The charging system may have failed and let the battery run down
result.now: Don't count on it restarting and running. Have it towed to a shop or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If a jump gets it running, it will likely die again within minutes. Don't drive it in traffic.
If you smelled burning rubber or heard a squeal first, the drive belt may have broken.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the hood, get everyone out and away from the car.
result.why: If the alternator stops charging, the car runs on the battery alone. Lights dim, gauges act up, and then the engine shuts off once the battery is too low to keep it running. A shop will usually test the alternator, belt and cables before replacing anything.

causes.name: Failed alternator
causes.clues: The battery light came on before it died.

causes.name: Broken or slipping drive belt
causes.clues: Squealing, a burning rubber smell, or heavy steering.

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery or charging cable
causes.clues: Flickering lights, or it happened after a bump.

you: Look at the drive belt with the engine off.
Check the battery clamps for looseness or buildup.

result.title: A worn ignition switch may be cutting power
result.now: Don't drive it until the ignition switch is checked. Have it towed, and check your VIN for open safety recalls.
if: If there's an open recall, the dealer will fix it at no charge.
Until it's fixed, keep only the car key on the ring. A heavy key ring makes this worse.
result.why: A worn ignition switch can slip from Run to Accessory or Off when it's jostled. The engine shuts off, and on some cars the airbags may be disabled too. Some vehicles have had recalls for exactly this.

causes.name: Worn ignition switch
causes.clues: It happens over bumps or when the key is touched.

causes.name: Heavy key ring pulling on the key
causes.clues: Lots of keys or accessories hanging from the car key.

causes.name: Loose wiring connection at the switch
causes.clues: Dash lights flicker over bumps.

you: Ask a dealer for your brand to confirm which recalls are still open for your VIN.
Remove extra keys from the ring.

result.title: It may have run out of fuel
result.now: Get somewhere safe, add a few gallons of fuel, and try to restart. It may need several tries of a few seconds each to refill the fuel lines.
if: If the check engine light was flashing before it died, don't restart it; have it towed.
If it still won't start after adding fuel, the fuel pump may have been damaged. Have it towed.
If the gauge showed fuel left when it died, have the gauge checked so it doesn't happen again.
If it stalls again with fuel in the tank, don't rely on it in traffic. Have it checked before driving again.
If you smell raw fuel, don't try to restart it.
result.why: Sputtering and surging before a stall is a common sign of fuel starvation. When the tank is low, hard turns, hills or braking can slosh fuel away from the pickup and the engine starves.

causes.name: Out of fuel
causes.clues: The gauge was near empty or the low fuel light was on.

causes.name: Inaccurate fuel gauge
causes.clues: The gauge has read oddly before.

causes.name: Fuel pump struggling on a low tank
causes.clues: It sputters at low fuel levels even when there's some left.

you: Note how many miles you drove since the last fill-up.

result.title: Possibly a fuel delivery problem or a severe misfire
result.now: Don't drive it until it's checked. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic who can scan for trouble codes.
if: If the check engine light was flashing, the catalytic converter can be damaged by running it. Don't keep trying to drive it.
If you smell raw fuel, keep sparks and flames away and don't restart it.
result.why: Sputtering, surging or losing power before a stall usually means the engine wasn't getting enough fuel or wasn't burning it properly. A weak fuel pump, a clogged filter or a bad sensor are common causes, and they tend to get worse. A shop will usually check codes and fuel pressure before replacing the pump.

causes.name: Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter
causes.clues: Worse going uphill or under hard acceleration, with no flashing light.

causes.name: Faulty airflow or throttle sensor
causes.clues: A steady check engine light, surging, or a rough idle.

causes.name: Severe misfire from an ignition coil or plugs
causes.clues: A flashing check engine light and shaking.

you: Note whether the check engine light was on or flashing.
Listen for the brief fuel pump hum from the rear when you turn the key to On.
shop: Code scan and live sensor data
Ignition coil and spark plug check

result.title: A failing sensor or electrical connection may be cutting the engine
result.now: Don't rely on it until it's diagnosed. Have it towed or have a mobile mechanic scan for trouble codes, even if no warning light is on.
if: If you're stuck somewhere unsafe and it restarts, move it only as far as a safe spot, then call for a tow.
If it only restarts after cooling down, tell the shop. That pattern often points to a heat-sensitive sensor.
result.why: An engine that cuts out instantly with no sputter has usually lost spark or the signal that controls it. A crankshaft position sensor that fails when hot is a common cause, and a shop will usually check codes and the sensor signal before replacing it. These problems come and go, so it may run fine for days before cutting out again.

causes.name: Failing crankshaft or camshaft position sensor
causes.clues: It dies suddenly when warm and restarts after cooling.

causes.name: Loose wiring, ground or fuel pump relay
causes.clues: It happens over bumps, or it restarts right away.

causes.name: Worn ignition switch
causes.clues: The dash lights blink off as it dies.

you: Write down when it happens: warm or cold, speed, bumps.
Ask a dealer for your brand to confirm which recalls are still open for your VIN.
shop: Code scan, including stored and pending codes
Crank and cam sensor signal test

result.title: A failed fuel pump or crankshaft sensor is possible
result.now: Stop cranking it. Have the car towed to a shop.
if: If a key or security light is flashing, try your spare key. The anti-theft system can block the engine from running.
If it restarts after sitting, don't count on it. These parts often fail completely soon after.
If you smell raw fuel, stop cranking and keep away from the car.
result.why: If the engine cranks normally but won't fire after dying on the road, it has usually lost fuel or spark. A fuel pump that stopped running and a crankshaft sensor that stopped reporting are common causes, and a shop will usually check fuses, relays and codes first.

causes.name: Failed fuel pump
causes.clues: No hum from the rear when you turn the key to On.

causes.name: Failed crankshaft position sensor
causes.clues: It died suddenly with no sputter.

causes.name: Fuel pump relay or fuse
causes.clues: Sudden failure. These are quick to check first.

you: Listen for the fuel pump hum.
Look for a flashing key or security light.
shop: Code scan for crank and cam sensor codes
Fuel pump relay and fuse check

result.title: The car lost electrical power, possibly at the battery connection
result.now: Get to safety, then check whether a battery cable is loose or has come off. If you can't fix it on the spot, have it towed.
if: If tightening a loose clamp brings everything back, have the cables and fuses checked before you rely on the car again.
If you smell burning, don't touch the wiring. Step away and call for help.
result.why: When the engine and dash both go dead at once, the car has lost its main power. A loose or corroded battery cable is a common cause. A blown main fuse or a failed ignition switch can do the same.

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery cable
causes.clues: A clamp that moves by hand, or it happened over a bump.

causes.name: Blown main fuse or fusible link
causes.clues: Cables are tight but there's still no power.

causes.name: Failed ignition switch
causes.clues: Power comes and goes when you move the key.

you: With the engine off, check that both battery clamps are tight.

result.title: Have it diagnosed before you drive it again
result.now: Have the car towed to a shop or call a mobile mechanic to scan it where it sits.
if: If a warning light came on, tell the shop which one. It narrows things down quickly.
If you smell fuel or burning, don't try to restart it.
result.why: An engine that shuts off while moving can stall again at a worse moment, like in an intersection or on a highway. The cause can be fuel, spark, electrical or overheating, and a scan plus a few tests will usually show which.

causes.name: Fuel delivery problem
causes.clues: Sputtering or loss of power first.

causes.name: Sensor or ignition failure
causes.clues: It cut out suddenly with no warning.

causes.name: Charging system failure
causes.clues: The battery light came on or the lights dimmed.

you: Write down what happened just before it died.
Check your VIN for open recalls.
